findings.title: Security group exposes an administrative port to the internet
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 5.2 - No security group ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote administration ports
findings.explanation: SSH is reachable from every address on the internet. This is the most scanned port on AWS and the usual first step in a host compromise.

findings.title: Security group exposes all TCP ports to the internet
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 5.2 - No security group ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote administration ports
findings.remediation_template:
# Remove the 0-65535 ingress block entirely.
# Open only the ports the service actually needs.
findings.explanation: A rule opening ports 0-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0 makes every other ingress restriction on the group meaningless.

findings.title: S3 bucket has a public ACL
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 2.1.5 - Configure S3 Block Public Access (bucket settings)
findings.explanation: A public-read ACL exposes every object in the bucket to anonymous requests.

findings.title: IAM policy grants wildcard action on wildcard resource
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 1.16 - No IAM policies granting full *:* administrative privileges
findings.explanation: Action "*" on Resource "*" is administrator access, so a single compromised workload becomes full account control.

findings.title: RDS instance is publicly accessible
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 2.3.3 - Ensure public access is not given to RDS instances
findings.explanation: The production database has a public endpoint, so its only protection is the security group in front of it.

findings.title: Security group exposes RDP to the internet
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 5.2 - No security group ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote administration ports
findings.explanation: RDP open to the world is continuously scanned and brute-forced, and exposes the service to protocol-level vulnerabilities regardless of password strength.

findings.title: S3 bucket has no public access block
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 2.1.5 - Configure S3 Block Public Access (bucket settings)
findings.remediation_template:
resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "sensitive_data" {
  bucket                  = aws_s3_bucket.sensitive_data.id
  block_public_acls       = true
  block_public_policy     = true
  ignore_public_acls      = true
  restrict_public_buckets = true
}
findings.explanation: Nothing prevents a future ACL or bucket policy from making this bucket public again. The block is the control that survives human error.

findings.title: S3 bucket has no server-side encryption
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 2.1.1 - Ensure all S3 buckets employ encryption-at-rest
findings.explanation: Objects are stored unencrypted while another bucket in the same file is encrypted, which is drift rather than a deliberate choice.

findings.title: CloudTrail is not multi-region
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 3.1 - Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
findings.explanation: Activity outside the trail's region is unrecorded, and attackers routinely operate in unused regions for exactly that reason.

findings.title: RDS storage is not encrypted
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 2.3.1 - Ensure encryption is enabled for RDS instances
findings.explanation: Volumes and automated snapshots are unencrypted, and this cannot be fixed in place — it needs a snapshot, an encrypted copy and a restore.

findings.title: S3 bucket versioning disabled
findings.cis_control: Not in CIS AWS Foundations 1.5.0 - AWS hardening: enable S3 bucket versioning
findings.explanation: Without versioning an overwrite or deletion is unrecoverable, whether accidental or from ransomware.

findings.title: S3 access logging disabled
findings.cis_control: Not in CIS AWS Foundations 1.5.0 - AWS hardening: enable S3 server access logging
findings.explanation: No record exists of who read objects from this bucket, so an exploited public ACL leaves no trail.

findings.title: KMS key rotation disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 3.8 - Ensure rotation for customer-created KMS keys is enabled
findings.explanation: Key material never changes, so a key compromised at any point stays useful indefinitely. Rotation is automatic and needs no application change.

findings.title: RDS backup retention below policy minimum
findings.cis_control: Not in CIS AWS Foundations 1.5.0 - AWS hardening: keep RDS backup retention at 7 days or more
findings.explanation: A single day of automated backups means a problem found on Monday morning may already be unrecoverable.

findings.title: CloudTrail log file validation disabled
findings.cis_control: CIS AWS 1.5.0 3.2 - Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
findings.explanation: Without validation there is no way to prove log files were not altered after delivery, which undermines their value as evidence.

attack_paths.name: Administrative port exposure to privilege escalation
attack_paths.narrative: An administrative port is exposed to the internet, and security groups lack restrictive ingress. This allows an attacker to reach the  infrastructure and leverage a wildcard IAM policy to escalate to full  account administrative privileges.

break_chain.why: Restricting wildcard permissions in IAM policies prevents an attacker from using an exposed port to escalate to full administrative control.

attack_paths.name: Public storage access to data exfiltration
attack_paths.narrative: A bucket has a public ACL and lacks a Public Access Block, allowing  anonymous read access. Because the data is unencrypted and access  logging is disabled, an attacker can exfiltrate sensitive data  without leaving a trace.

break_chain.why: Enabling Block Public Access at the bucket level acts as a global  guardrail that overrides any accidental public ACLs or policies.

attack_paths.name: Public database exposure to data theft
attack_paths.narrative: The database is publicly accessible and the surrounding security  groups are overly permissive. Combined with unencrypted storage,  an attacker can directly target the database endpoint to exfiltrate  the entire dataset.

break_chain.why: Disabling public accessibility for the RDS instance removes the  direct internet path, forcing all traffic through secure internal  network controls.
